title: ESP32 deep sleep and timer wake-up

questions.prompt: Which option states the main idea of “ESP32 deep sleep and timer wake-up” correctly?
options: A USB-C connector does not mean the chip supports USB HID.
A Hall sensor detects magnetic fields.
Many ESP32 boards have no built-in RGB LED.
Deep sleep reduces power use in battery-powered ESP32 devices that wait for long periods.
questions.answer: Deep sleep reduces power use in battery-powered ESP32 devices that wait for long periods.
questions.explanation: Deep sleep reduces power use in battery-powered ESP32 devices that wait for long periods.

questions.prompt: Which additional fact about “ESP32 deep sleep and timer wake-up” is accurate?
options: Older original ESP32 chips had an internal Hall sensor and legacy APIs
Most CPU and RAM state is lost
Where present, the LED may be addressable or a discrete RGB part with different pin/driver wiring.
Some boards use a USB-to-serial bridge only for flashing.
questions.answer: Most CPU and RAM state is lost
questions.explanation: Most CPU and RAM state is lost

questions.prompt: Which practical detail should be considered when using “ESP32 deep sleep and timer wake-up”?
options: families such as ESP32-S2/S3/C3 do not have the same integrated sensor.
selected RTC memory and wake sources can remain available.
Certain ESP32-S2/S3 boards with native USB OTG can expose CDC and HID
`RGB_BUILTIN` and `rgbLedWrite` require a supporting Arduino-ESP32 version and board.
questions.answer: selected RTC memory and wake sources can remain available.

questions.prompt: Which statement from the “ESP32 deep sleep and timer wake-up” lesson is correct?
options: verify the exact board and Arduino core configuration.
